title: Protocol for the production and purification of an i-Motif-specific nanobody
protocol: Streak bacteria from Addgene on a LB-kanamycin agar plate and grow overnight at 37°C upside down to avoid condensation.
Select five colonies to inoculate into five separate 5 mL LB-kanamycin cultures and grow overnight at 37°C while shaking at 230 RPM.
Purify the plasmids using a miniprep kit and store at −20°C.
Transform BL21(DE3) competent E. coli cells with pSANG10-3F-iMbody plasmids prepared in Step 1.
Add 50 ng of each purified plasmid to 25 μL of competent cells separately.
Gently mix by flicking the tubes.
Incubate on ice for 30 min.
Perform a heat shock by incubating the tubes at 42°C for 30 s.
Incubate on ice for 5 min.
Add 250 μL LB broth (without kanamycin) to each tube.
Incubate at 37°C while shaking at 230 RPM for 1 h.
Spread each mixture on a prewarmed LB-kanamycin agar plate.
Let the plates air-dry on the bench.
Grow overnight (16–24 h) at 37°C with the plates upside down to avoid condensation.
Pick one colony from each transformed BL21 plate to inoculate five separate 10 mL LB-kanamycin cultures.
Grow overnight (16–24 h) at 37°C while shaking at 230 RPM.
Add 250 μL glycerol to 1 mL overnight culture in a cryovial tube.
Mix thoroughly and store at -80°C.
Purify plasmids from remaining 9 mL overnight culture using a miniprep kit.
Store purified plasmids at -20°C.
Sequence iMbody utilizing T7 promoter forward and T7 terminal reverse primers.
Proceed to Step 4 if the iMbody sequence is confirmed.
Discard unverified minipreps if the sequence is not confirmed.
Repeat Steps 2 and 3 for unverified transformations.
Inoculate 50 mL of LB-kanamycin broth with bacteria from a verified glycerol stock.
Grow overnight culture at 37°C while shaking at 230 RPM.
Inoculate 990 mL of LB-kanamycin broth with 10 mL of the overnight culture.
Grow culture at 37°C while shaking at 230 RPM.
Measure optical density at 600 nm initially after 1 hour.
Measure optical density every 10 minutes thereafter.
Induce expression of iMbody when OD600nm reaches ∼0.4–0.5 by adding 1 mL of 1 M IPTG.
Continue growing culture at 30°C while shaking at 230 RPM for 24 hours.
Reduce the temperature from 37°C to 30°C.
Add 0.5 mL of 1 M IPTG to reinduce iMbody expression.
Incubate at 30°C and shake at 230 RPM for 24 hours.
Divide the culture into three 500 mL polypropylene bottles.
Centrifuge at 10,000 × g for 30 minutes at 4°C.
Filter the supernatant using a vacuum filter system with a 0.22-μm filter.
Discard the pellets.
Store the filtered supernatant at 4°C for up to one week before purification.
Shake the Ni-NTA agarose resins container well.
Transfer 0.5 mL of Ni-NTA resins to a 15 mL tube.
Wash the resins twice with 10 mL DPBS.
Resuspend the resin pellet in 1 mL DPBS and add it to the filtered supernatant.
Incubate for 1 hour at 4°C on a roller at 40 RPM.
Prepare a gravity-flow chromatography column by running two CV ddH2O and one CV DPBS through the column.
Flow the supernatant-Ni-NTA resins mixture through the column.
Collect the flow-through and store it at 4°C until SDS-PAGE gel analysis.
Close the gravity-flow column.
Incubate the resins with 30 mL of NPI-20 buffer in the column for 10 minutes.
Open the column and collect the NPI-20.
Add the collected NPI-20 to the flow-through.
Incubate resins in the column with 5 mL of NPI-500 buffer for 5 minutes.
Collect the eluted iMbody from the column.
Measure the absorbance at 280 nm (A280nm).
Continue collecting fractions until A280nm value drops below 0.02.
Combine all collected fractions in a 50 mL tube.
Keep the combined tube on ice after measurement.
Incubate resins with 20 mL of NPI-500 buffer for 20 minutes.
Dispose of the NPI-500 buffer according to toxic material handling guidelines.
Incubate resins with 30 mL of 0.5 M NaOH for 30 minutes in the gravity-column.
Flow-through and discard the NaOH solution.
Wash the resins with 1 CV ddH2O after washing with NaOH.
Close the gravity-flow column, collect the resins using 10 mL of 20% ethanol.
Incubate resins to appear bluish before use.
Store regenerated Ni-NTA agarose resins at 4°C for several months if needed.
Rinse the gravity-flow column with ddH2O.
Equilibrate an Amicon ultra-15 centrifugal filter unit using 10 mL of DBPS supplemented with 10% glycerol.
Add 5 mL DPBS-glycerol to the Amicon tube.
Top up with 10 mL of eluted iMbody sample.
Centrifuge at 3000 × g and 4°C for 7 minutes.
Collect the flow-through.
Top up with more iMbody sample.
Repeat the process until no iMbody sample remains.
Top up the remaining iMbody sample in the Amicon tube with DPBS-glycerol.
Centrifuge at 3000 × g and 4°C for 7 minutes.
Repeat Step 9-d until 50 mL of flow-through is achieved.
Ensure the exchange of NPI-500 buffer with DPBS-glycerol.
Continue the centrifugation until the upper chamber contains between 0.5 mL to 1 mL of concentrated sample.
Equilibrate two Costar Spin-X centrifuge tubes with DPBS-glycerol.
Transfer the concentrated iMbody sample to Costar Spin-X centrifuge tubes.
Centrifuge for 1 minute at 10,000 × g and 4°C.
Measure A280nm to determine the concentration of iMbody.
Run an SDS-PAGE to check the purity of purified iMbody.
Add 2 μg iMbody to a tube.
Add 4 μL NuPAGE LDS sample buffer to the tube.
Add 2 μL NuPAGE sample reducing agent to the tube.
Add up to 16 μL molecular biology grade water into the tube.
Heat the sample at 95°C for 5 minutes.
Load the sample on a NuPAGE 4%–12% Bis-Tris mini protein gel.
Load 7 μL of prestained protein ladder in a separate well.
Perform electrophoresis at 200 V using MES-SDS running buffer for 60 minutes or until well-separated ladder bands appear on the gel.
Rinse the gel using ddH2O.
Stain the gel using 15 mL EZBlue gel staining reagent for 1 hour at room temperature with gentle orbital shaking.
Destain extensively using ddH2O overnight (16–24 hours) or until the blue background is faded at room temperature with gentle orbital shaking.
Dispense the purified iMbody sample into 50 μL aliquots.
Store the aliquoted samples at -80°C.
Order 5′ Biotin-TEG conjugated DNA oligonucleotides as lyophilized samples.
Reconstitute the oligonucleotide in nuclease-free water to make a 100 μM stock solution.
Vortex thoroughly.
If resuspension is difficult, heat the tube at 55°C for 10 minutes followed by vortexing and centrifugation.
Measure the concentration and purity of the stock solution.
Dilute an iM-forming oligonucleotide in 200 mM Tris-HCl pH 6 to a final concentration of 70 nM.
Prepare a 60 μL DNA solution for each well and ensure at least duplicates for each condition.
Anneal the oligonucleotide by heating at 95°C for 10 minutes followed by slowly cooling down to room temperature (∼22°C).
Keep the annealed oligonucleotide at 4°C overnight (16–24 hours).
Coat a 96-well Nunc MaxiSorp plate by adding 50 μL per well of 50 μg/mL NeutrAvidin diluted in DPBS.
Shake the plate gently, seal it with a SealPlate film, and incubate overnight (16–24 hours) at 4°C.
Aspirate the contents from the plate after incubation.
Wash the plate one time with DPBS (250 μL per well).
Turn the plate upside down and gently tap on absorbent paper to eliminate any extra liquid.
Block the plate by adding 200 μL per well of DPBS supplemented with 2% BSA and 0.1% Tween 20.
Incubate the plate at room temperature (approximately 22°C) for 2 hours while shaking at 300 RPM.
Aspirate the blocking buffer from each well.
Wash one time with 200 mM Tris-HCl pH 6 or appropriate buffers (250 μL per well).
Turn the plate upside down and gently tap on absorbent paper to eliminate any extra liquid.
Add 60 μL of annealed DNA samples to each well.
Incubate at room temperature (approximately 22°C) for 1 hour while shaking at 300 RPM.
Aspirate the contents from each well after incubation.
Wash one time with DPBS (250 μL per well).
Turn the plate upside down and gently tap on absorbent paper to eliminate any extra liquid.
Thaw the required volume of iMbody based on its concentration determined after His-tag purification and the number of samples in the planned ELISA experiment.
Filter the thawed iMbody using a Costar Spin-X centrifuge tube.
Determine the concentration again following the instructions in Step 9.
Make a serial dilution of iMbody starting from 10 nM to 19.5 pM in DPBS supplemented with 5% BSA, 0.1% Tween 20, and 100 μg/mL salmon sperm DNA.
Incubate the diluted iMbody at room temperature (approximately 22°C) for 15 minutes.
Add 60 μL of serially diluted iMbody per well.
Incubate at room temperature (∼22°C) for 45 min while shaking at 300 RPM on a plate shaker.
Aspirate the contents and wash three times with DPBS supplemented with 0.1% Tween 20 and once with DPBS (250 μL per well).
After each washing, turn the plate upside down and gently tap on absorbent paper to eliminate any extra liquid.
Dilute the HRP-conjugated anti-FLAG antibody 1:15000 in DPBS supplemented with 2% BSA, 0.1% Tween 20.
Incubate at room temperature (∼22°C) for 15 min.
Add 50 μL diluted HRP-conjugated anti-FLAG antibody per well and incubate at room temperature (∼22°C) for 45 min while shaking at 300 RPM on a plate shaker.
Aspirate the contents and wash twice with DPBS supplemented with 0.1% Tween 20 and once with DPBS (250 μL per well).
After each washing, turn the plate upside down and gently tap on absorbent paper to eliminate any extra liquid.
Add 50 μL of TMB substrate solution to each well and incubate at room temperature (∼22°C) with occasional gentle shaking until a dark blue color develops for the highest concentration of iMbody.
Stop the reaction by adding 50 μL of 0.5 M HCl per well.
Read the absorbance at 450 nm using a UV-vis plate reader within 10 min of adding HCl.
Make the graph in GraphPad Prism.
Check problem 3 in the troubleshooting section if significant cross-reactivity with negative controls is observed.
Anneal iM-forming oligonucleotide in the presence of SWNT-COOH dispersed in DMF at final concentrations of 5, 10, and 20 μg/mL.
Include a control sample containing only DMF.
Prepare coverslips for cell culture.
Submerge glass coverslips in 1 M HCl.
Incubate coverslips in 1 M HCl at room temperature (approximately 22°C) for at least 3 hours.
Rinse the coverslips three times with distilled water (ddH2O).
Rinse the coverslips three times with pure ethanol.
Air dry the coverslips in a biosafety cabinet.
Place each coverslip into an individual well of a 12-well plate containing 1 mL of 0.001% poly-L-lysine solution.
Incubate the coverslips at room temperature (approximately 22°C) for 20 minutes.
Aspirate the poly-L-lysine solution from each well.
Rinse each coverslip with 1 mL molecular biology grade water per well.
Air dry the coverslips in a biosafety cabinet.
Sterilize the coverslips under UV light in a biosafety cabinet for at least 1 hour.
Grow HeLa cells in a T75 cell culture flask using DMEM supplemented with 10% FBS and 1% penicillin-streptomycin until they reach 70-80% confluency.
Rinse the cells twice with 15 mL of warm (approximately 37°C) DPBS.
Add 4 mL of warm (approximately 37°C) trypsin-EDTA to the flask and incubate at 37°C for 5 minutes or until all cells are detached.
Add 8 mL of warm (approximately 37°C) complete media to the flask to deactivate trypsin.
Collect the cells into a 15 mL tube.
Centrifuge the cell suspension for 1 minute at 500 × g at room temperature (approximately 22°C).
Discard the supernatant.
Gently resuspend the cells with up to 1 mL complete media.
Count the number of cells using a hemocytometer.
Keep the tube containing the remaining cells in a 37°C water bath.
Seed 1 × 10^4 cells resuspended in 1 mL complete media in each well that contains poly-L-lysine coated coverslip.
Incubate the cells at 37°C and 5% CO2 until they reach 70%-80% confluency, which may take 1–2 days after seeding.
Pre-fix the cells by adding 1 mL of 1% formaldehyde diluted in DPBS directly to the well containing media and incubating for 2 min at room temperature (∼22°C).
Aspirate the content.
Rinse the cells once with 1 mL ice-cold DPBS per well.
Fix the cells by adding 1 mL 1% formaldehyde in each well and incubating for 15 min at 4°C without shaking.
Rinse the cells twice with 1 mL ice-cold DPBS per well.
Permeabilize the cells by adding 1 mL of ice-cold 0.1% Triton X-100 diluted in DPBS in each well and incubating for 15 min at 4°C without shaking.
Rinse the cells twice with 1 mL ice-cold DPBS per well.
Block the coverslip and cells with 1 mL DPBS supplemented with 2% BSA, 1% skim milk, 0.1% Tween 20, and 0.01% Triton X in blocking buffer for 3 h at 4°C.
Thaw the required volume of iMbody based on concentration determined after His-tag purification.
Filter the thawed iMbody using a Costar Spin-X centrifuge tube.
Determine the concentration of filtered iMbody again.
Prepare a serial dilution of iMbody ranging from 2 μM to 500 nM in blocking buffer.
Aspirate the blocking buffer from each well.
Dispense 350 μL per well of the diluted iMbody.
Incubate overnight (16–20 hours) at 4°C.
Perform four washes on cells using 1 mL ice-cold DPBS supplemented with 0.1% Tween 20 per well, each lasting for 5 minutes and involving gentle shaking at 200 RPM.
Rinse the cells with 1 mL ice-cold DPBS per well.
Dilute rabbit anti-FLAG antibody in blocking buffer to a concentration of 1:600.
Dispense 350 μL of diluted secondary antibody per well.
Incubate for 30 minutes at room temperature (∼22°C) while shaking at 200 RPM.
Perform two washes on cells using 1 mL ice-cold DPBS supplemented with 0.1% Tween 20 per well, each lasting for 5 minutes and involving gentle shaking at 200 RPM.
Rinse the cells with 1 mL ice-cold DPBS per well.
Dispense 350 μL of Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-rabbit at a 1:400 dilution and Alexa Fluor 555-conjugated phalloidin at a 1:20 dilution per well, diluted in blocking buffer.
Cover the plate with aluminum foil.
Incubate the plate at room temperature (approximately 22°C) for 30 minutes while shaking at 200 RPM on a plate shaker.
Wash the cells twice using 1 mL of ice-cold DPBS supplemented with 0.1% Tween 20 per well, each wash lasting 5 minutes and involving shaking at 200 RPM on a plate shaker.
Rinse the cells twice with 1 mL per well of molecular biology grade water.
Remove the coverslip from the plate carefully.
Place the coverslip onto a paper towel to air dry within a biosafety cabinet, ensuring the side with attached cells does not touch the paper towel.
Dispense 15 μL of ProLong Gold antifade reagent with DAPI onto the center of a slide.
Mount the coverslip onto the slide with the side containing attached cells facing downward and making contact with the mounting reagent.
Store the slides in a cassette within a dark location at room temperature (approximately 22°C) overnight for 16–24 hours.
Seal the edge of the coverslip with nail polish.
Transfer the slides to a storage environment at 4°C protected from light for long-term storage.
Acquire images on a Leica TCS SP8 confocal microscope using a 63×/1.40 oil (HC PL APO CS2) objective or similar.
Use a 405 nm laser with 3% power to excite and image DAPI for nuclei.
Use a 488 nm laser with 50% power to excite and image Alexa Fluor 488 for iMs.
Use a 561 nm laser with 5% power to excite and image Alexa Fluor 555 for actin filaments.
Identify the cell boundary using actin filaments and zoom in when investigating individual cells.
Maintain consistent frame size when examining iM formation under various conditions.
Determine the required number of z-stacks and intervals using the “system optimized” setting.
Navigate to the brightest image in blue (nucleus) channel and choose “Auto” in the B&C pop up.
Navigate to the brightest image in red (F-actin) channel and choose “Auto” in the B&C pop up.
Navigate to the brightest image in green (iMs) channel and choose the “Auto” option in the B&C pop-up.
Refine the “Minimum” setting until distinct foci become visible.
Refine the “Maximum” setting until there is no background interference.
Maintain a consistent “Minimum” and “Maximum” setting for different concentrations of iMbody used in immunostaining.
Maintain a consistent “Minimum” and “Maximum” setting when examining the impact of various treatments or conditions on iM formation.
Smooth the channels (optional).
Merge the channels.
Create a composite while keeping the source images.
